direction: Original botanical scenes with reduced detail and strict low-relief clay typography

Use case: stylized-concept.
Edit target: the supplied ORIGINAL botanical clay report illustration. Make a final wide report banner in precisely its established burgundy, cream, sage, ochre, terracotta and soft-blue palette. Keep the ORIGINAL IDEA and sculpted material, camera and warm lighting.
Output format: very wide landscape banner, 1536 x 640, about 2.4:1. Entire canvas is one quiet matte deep-burgundy clay surface. Fill the full canvas; no outer margin, border or separate vignette.
Simplification level: retain the recognizable original small scene and its meaning, but reduce detail by about two thirds. Use bold broad forms: a handful of large leaves, a simple trunk, a smooth earth base, clean water shapes. REMOVE scattered pebbles, acorns, tiny plants, leaf litter, granular soil, fine bark texture, many roots, footprints and decorative debris. Visible clay with gentle tool marks; no rough photorealistic textures.
Typography: cream-colored sculpted clay Cyrillic lettering with STRICT, QUIET, professional geometric sans-serif shapes. Conventional regular proportions, medium-bold weight, consistent stroke widths, upright straight stems, straight aligned baselines, clean flat faces and very shallow relief. Slightly softened edges only. NO puffy inflated lettering, playful hand lettering, slanted or wavy baselines, exaggerated rounded cartoon letters or giant chunky letters.
Composition: compose the title and scene TOGETHER as a single restrained clay relief banner. The legible two-line title occupies the open left half, the botanical scene occupies the right half. The low smooth clay ground or path continues gently underneath both the title and illustration; it is their common foundation, not an underline ribbon. The title casts the SAME subtle shadows as the scene. The symbolic scene can lightly approach the title's empty margins but never cover the letter faces. Give both room to breathe, align them as one composition, no boxes or stickers behind the words. Title height on two lines must be at most 38 percent of the banner height; scene at most 72 percent. At least 7 percent safe margins. One visual story, restrained, consistent with the original project.
